analysis: Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 789-1039 and 1040-1380). No head text or patch hunk was supplied, so the actual PR change is not visible. I could not identify any added or removed line, and any security conclusion about the head revision is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The base text is documentation only and has no runtime behavior. It describes already-merged or candidate behavior: App Attest shadow rollout and protocol 3 (T-052..T-058, TB-011), SSD prefix cache disk budget and TTL (T-041), the profiler (T-051), and MDM/APNs recovery. The excerpts do not conflict with the canonical threat model. The changelog notes the SSD cache stays at the 15-minute TTL and 100 GiB history, while the canonical T-041 now records a 30-minute TTL since 2026-09-26. Those older entries are historical, so this is not a regression. Later passes should check whether the PR adds changelog claims that overstate security properties, for example calling App Attest authoritative, claiming physical uniqueness, or claiming runtime secrecy. They should also check the companion code changes in other units for interactions with TB-011/T-053/T-054 (final-dispatch authorization, build qualification) and T-041 (TTL and name derivation).
